headline: The STI fell 2.05% on Friday to 4,975, below 5,000 for the first time since June, and lost 4.9% in the week as a global AI and chip sell-off hit. Wall Street fell again Friday (Nasdaq -5.3%, Nvidia -14%), so expect a weak, volatile open. Oil is near $92, down about 20% this month.

sectors.why: No clear sector news; it will mostly follow the broad risk-off mood after the STI's 4.9% weekly fall.
Singtel fell only about 1% on Friday while the STI lost 2%; defensive telcos may hold up, but no specific news points either way.
No sector-specific news; weak global sentiment is a mild headwind.
US money moved into consumer staples during the sell-off, which can help defensives, but there is no Singapore-specific news.
3Q GDP showed food and beverage services weak; no new news since. Risk-off mood is a mild headwind.
Wholesale trade grew 8% in 3Q, but the AI sell-off may cool electronics trade flows; no clear direction.
Global AI and chip rout (Nvidia -14% Friday, Nasdaq -5.3%) and new US licence rules for advanced AI chips shipped to Singapore from 19 Nov weigh on SGX tech suppliers; Venture fell 3.3%.
Brent fell below $92, down nearly 20% in November and a third straight weekly drop, on a supply surplus (IEA about 2 mb/d) and record Hormuz flows.
Banks' 3Q was mixed (OCBC beat, DBS and UOB missed) with high SGD rates supporting income, but market falls hit wealth and trading fees; SGX fell 3.1% Friday. REITs face talk of a Fed hike.
Healthcare drew safe-haven money in the US sell-off, but no Singapore-specific news.
Defensive flows helped US healthcare; 3Q GDP showed biomedical manufacturing weak in Singapore. No clear direction.
Keppel fell 3.1% Friday in the broad sell-off; construction was strong in 3Q GDP, so the month-long picture is mixed.
No relevant news.
Gold rose as a safe haven, but no clear news for SGX-listed miners or materials.
3Q GDP showed chemicals manufacturing weak; falling oil lowers feedstock costs. No clear direction.
Seatrium fell 8.8% Friday, the STI's worst; sliding oil prices and forced selling hit offshore and marine names, though 3Q transport engineering was strong.
3Q GDP showed retail trade weak; no new news since.
US AI chip licence rules may slow some Singapore data-centre work and AI sentiment is poor, but SGX has few listed tech-services firms; mild headwind only.
Lower oil helps airline costs, but SATS fell 5.3% Friday in the sell-off; the two pull in opposite directions.
Defensive sector that may draw money in a risk-off market; no specific news.
